text: In the ridge-regularization section, what happens as λ is made too small (λ→0) versus too large (λ→∞)?
choices: Too small → OLS that overfits noise (high variance); too large → weights shrink to 0 (underfit)
Too small → weights shrink to 0; too large → overfits training noise
Both extremes give identical, minimal test error
λ only affects training speed, not the bias-variance tradeoff
explanation: Section 8.7: λ→0 recovers ordinary least squares, which memorizes noise (high variance); λ→∞ drives ŵ→0 (maximum bias, underfitting). The optimal λ*>0 balances the two. Option 1 reverses the two limits.
